text: . Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like Give It Up Campaign.The Give It Up campaign, launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2015, has encouraged consumers to voluntarily give up their LPG subsidies. Under the campaign, more than one crore 13 lakh LPG consumers have voluntarily surrendered their LPG subsidy. The savings helped provide LPG connections to poor households under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, particularly benefiting rural women who relied on firewood and cow dung for cooking. The government has provided over ten crore 56 lakh free LPG connections under the scheme to adult women from poor households across the country. Addressing the Delhi Economics Conclave in 2015, Prime Minister Modi highlighted that the Give It Up movement inspired the citizens to come together to help underprivileged families acquire clean fuel.A resident of Uttar Pradesh, Sanju Devi said that the gas stove has made cooking much more convenient and freed her from exposure to smoke.The Give It Up campaign has promoted a sense of social responsibility among citizens and has supported the government’s efforts to ensure clean cooking fuel access for all.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah today spoke with the Chief Ministers of Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry, Odisha and Chhattisgarh in the wake of Cyclone Arnab. Mr Shah assured them of every assistance to mitigate the hardship of the people in the face of the disaster.In a social media post, the Minister said that NDRF and SDRF teams have sprung into action and are continuing rescue and relief operations on a war footing. Mr Shah added that an Inter-Ministerial Central Team will soon be sent to these states to assess the impact and further assistance required. He said, Central government stands with the people with resolute commitment.

. India’s industrial output, as measured by the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), grew by 6.7 per cent on an annual basis in September this year. However, the industrial activity slowed on month on month basis, easing from a downwardly revised IIP growth of 7.8 per cent in August.According to the data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation today, electricity and gas supply recorded strong growth of 11.2 per cent in September, while manufacturing, which carries the heaviest weight in the index, expanded by 7.6 per cent. Water supply, sewerage and waste management also registered healthy growth of 5.8 per cent. In contrast, the mining sector remained a laggard, contracting by 6.2 per cent during the period under review.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices today ended half a percent down. The Sensex dropped 353 points to close at 73,246. The Nifty also slipped 51 points to settle at 22,699.In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index advanced over 0.4 per cent, and the Smallcap 100 index jumped 0.9 per cent.In the Sensex pack, 21 out of 30 constituent companies registered losses. Among the top underperformers, Reliance dropped nearly three and a half per cent, Infosys slipped over 3.3 per cent, and Tech Mahindra fell by more than 1.8 per cent. In contrast, Larsen and Toubro rose 3.7 per cent, Trent gained 2.8 per cent, and SBI advanced over 1.2 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 18 out of 28 sectors ended in the positive territory. Among the top movers, Hospitals rose almost 1.6 per cent, Auto gained over 1.3 per cent, and Mid-Small Private Banks advanced 1.3 per cent. Conversely, Energy shed nearly 2.3 per cent, Oil and Gas as well as  Telecommunication lost 2.1 per cent, and IT declined almost 1.8 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2,245 companies advanced, 2 thousand and 79 declined and 231 remained unchanged.

. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold rose 0.9 per cent to 1,42,707 rupees per 10 Meanwhile, silver was half a per cent up at 1,93, 442 rupees per kilogram, according to the closing rates from the India Bullion and Jewellers Association.

. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Ministry of Education and UNESCO today exchanged a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to take clean sport values to classrooms across India through the ‘Sports Values in Every Classroom Toolkit’. The MoU was exchanged in the presence of Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi, Director of UNESCO’s Regional Office for South Asia, Dr Tim Curtis.Addressing the event, Mr joshi said that the MoU would help address the longstanding gap between education and sports. He also said that students who performed well academically did not always participate in sports, and emphasised the need to strengthen grassroots opportunities and build better pathways for young athletes.Meanwhile, Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya said that sporting excellence and sporting integrity must go hand in hand. He added that talent, discipline and hard work are essential for sporting success, but integrity, fairness and credibility are equally important.The initiative is aimed at embedding values such as respect, integrity and fairness in children through education, sports and everyday classroom activities. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the toolkit’s video modules will be made available in 13 Indian languages, with the objective of reaching students across the country and building a stronger, fairer sporting ecosystem.

. India has said at the FATF meeting underway in Paris that terror financing and cross border terrorism need to be held accountable. Briefing media in New Delhi yesterday, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, the world needs to do more so that terrorism in all its forms and manifestations can be fought harder and defeated by the global community.On the West Asia conflict, the spokesperson expressed India’s deep concern about the ongoing conflict in the region. He informed that 22 Indian nationals have died in the conflict, including 14 seafarers. He said India remains in close touch with the community in the Gulf region for their safety and well-being. He said that three Indians have lost their lives in Saudi Arabia.Mr Jaiswal also informed that External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar will be attending the G 20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta, US from tomorrow. On the sidelines, Dr Jaishankar will also participate in a QUAD Foreign Ministers Meeting. He will also have several bilateral engagements with his counterparts.Mr Jaiswal informed that from Atlanta, the External Affairs Minister will travel to St John’s, Antigua and Barbuda to lead the Indian delegation for the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting to be held from 1st to 4th November. The theme of the forthcoming CHOGM is “Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth”.

. Major Asian stock indices surged today. South Korea’s Kospi skyrocketed over 6.6 per cent, Taiwan’s Taiex index rose two per cent, Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained 1.1 per cent, China’s Shanghai Composite jumped 0.9 per cent, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng climbed over 0.2 per cent, while Singapore’s Strait Times ended on a flat note.In European markets, Germany’s DAX climbed 0.2 per cent, while London’s FTSE 100 dipped 0.2 per cent, when reports last came in.

. In Men’s Cricket, India defeated hosts New Zealand by six wickets in the third T-20 International at Wellington today, taking an unassailable three-nil lead in the five-match series. Chasing a target of 199 runs, India stormed to victory in just 13-point-two overs, losing four wickets. Abhishek Sharma led the charge with a sensational 113 off just 38 balls, while his opening partner, Vaibhav Suryavanshi, smashed a quickfire 45 off 19 deliveries.Earlier, New Zealand posted 198 for the loss of three wickets in their stipulated 20 overs. Daryl Mitchell finished unbeaten on 89 of 52 balls, while Finn Allen contributed 40. Arshdeep Singh, Axar Patel and Nitish Reddy claimed one wicket each for India. Abhishek Sharma was named Player of the Match for his match-winning knock.

. The India Meteorological Centre (IMD) has said that a well marked low pressure area over Eastcentral and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal persisted over the region today.It is most likely to persist over the region and intensify into a depression today. It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a deep depression tomorrow and into a cyclonic storm over the Westcentral Bay of Bengal by Monday morning.Under the influence of likely formation of cyclonic storm over the Westcentral Bay of Bengal by Monday and its further intensification, isolated extremely heavy rainfall is expected  over Coastal Andhra Pradesh on Tuesday and Wednesday and  further over Odisha and Telangana on Wednesday.IMD has issued red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal tomorrow.The Met Department has forecast Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep and South Interior Karnataka will experience heavy rainfall tomorrow. The weather agency has said that thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds is likely over East Madhya Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh tomorrow.

. India stormed into the semifinals of the inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship with a 48-20 win over Tanzania in Ahmedabad yesterday, extending their unbeaten run to five matches. The semifinal is scheduled for Friday. India, assured of a top finish in the group stage, have one match remaining against Sri Lanka tomorrow.In the women’s competition, Kenya defeated Scotland 61-16 to maintain their unbeaten run, while Malaysia thrashed Singapore 62-17. Elsewhere, Bangladesh beat Singapore 60-28, with Mijanur Rahman scoring 12 points and Dipayon Golder contributing 10 points. Canada defeated Scotland 62-30 for their second win of the tournament, with Anmol Thakur and Manpreet Singh scoring 19 and 15 points, respectively.

. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath held detailed discussions with a 14-member high-level business delegation from Singapore in Lucknow yesterday.Led by the Singapore Business Federation, the delegation expressed interest in making substantial investments in strategic sectors such as logistics, semiconductors, data centres, green energy, urban planning and hospitality. The delegation is visiting Uttar Pradesh following the Chief Minister’s visit to Singapore in February.Chief Minister Yogi proposed developing a dedicated ‘Singapore City’ and a high-tech industrial township near the Noida International Airport at Jewar. He said that the region, situated at the confluence of the Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight Corridors and connected to a world-class expressway network, had the potential to emerge as a major supply chain hub for international companies in northern India.The Chief Minister highlighted that the six strategic nodes of the UP Defence Industrial Corridor, located in Lucknow, Kanpur, Jhansi, Agra, Aligarh and Chitrakoot, have received investment proposals worth more than 35,000 crore rupees.

. Cyclone Arnab has caused extensive damage to crops, houses, roads and power infrastructure across several districts of Andhra Pradesh. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has requested the Centre to send an inter-ministerial team for an early assessment of the losses. The State Government has intensified relief and restoration operations in the affected areas.Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu reviewed cyclone relief operations through the State’s Real-Time Governance Centre and directed officials to expedite restoration of essential services. The Chief Minister announced an ex-gratia of five lakh rupees each to the families of those who lost their lives and financial assistance to affected households. Preliminary estimates indicate damage to over 70 thousand hectares of paddy and more than 10 thousand hectares of horticultural crops.Over 28 thousand people have been evacuated to relief shelters, with NDRF and SDRF teams deployed across affected districts. Electricity restoration is progressing, with nearly 80 percent of power supply restored in Visakhapatnam district. Repair work is continuing in Konaseema, Kakinada and the Godavari districts, where fallen trees and damaged electricity poles disrupted services. Officials are also clearing blocked roads and restoring drinking water supplies. Meanwhile, the Chief Minister has requested Centre to send a team to assess cyclone-related losses.

. Indian Railways has announced 1,265 vacancies for Station Master posts across various Railway Recruitment Boards and zones, opening up new employment opportunities for graduate candidates. The Railways Ministry said that in an important recruitment-related decision, the Railway Board has prescribed that Station Master recruitment will be notified separately from 2026 onwards. The dedicated recruitment process provides candidates with a specific notification covering eligibility requirements, examination procedures and vacancy distribution for the post. The online application window will remain open till 25th of next month. Candidates are advised to review the detailed eligibility conditions, vacancy distribution and application instructions before submitting their forms. The recruitment reflects Indian Railways’ continued efforts to provide career opportunities to eligible candidates while strengthening its operational workforce.

. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh held a bilateral meeting with the Minister of National Defence of the Republic of Korea, Kang Shin-chul, on the sidelines of the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus  (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu, Philippines yesterday. The Defence Ministry said, during the comprehensive talks, both leaders reviewed the expanding defence cooperation between the two countries.Emphasising the shared vision for an open, free, and inclusive region, Mr Singh and Mr Shin-chul deliberated on concrete pathways to strengthen security in the Indo-Pacific. They also expressed mutual satisfaction over the strengthening of strategic partnerships. Furthermore, they engaged in detailed discussions on exploring new opportunities to co-develop military technologies, enhance joint industry collaborations, and promote robust maritime security.The Ministry said that ADMM-Plus meeting remains a premier platform for ASEAN member states and its eight dialogue partners, including India and South Korea, to reinforce security and strategic cooperation.

. Union Minister of Road, Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari has said with a value of 22 lakh crore rupees India’s automobile industry has overtaken Japan to become 3rd largest automobile industry in the world. The Minister expressed confidence that with this growth the India’s automobile Industry will become largest automobile Industry in the world the next 5 years.Addressing a conclave organised by a private news organisation in New Delhi, Mr Gadkari said that with the construction of good roads across the country, the logistics cost of India has decreased by 6 per cent. Mr Gadkari emphasised that the construction of expressways and highways has not only reduced travel time but also contributed to the economic and infrastructural development of areas surrounding these highways.The Minister further said that Indian farmers are becoming important players in the production of Hydrogen and other valuable energy products and contributing in reducing India’s need for importing these materials. Mr Gadkari also said that with increasing Hydrogen production, India can become an energy exporting country in the future.

. In the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by seven paise to close at Rs 95.12 against the US dollar.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 102.18 in intra-day trade.

. The third season of the Nepal Premier League, Nepal’s premier franchise-based T20 cricket tournament, begins today at the Tribhuvan University International Cricket Ground in Kirtipur. The tournament will continue until November 21, with eight franchises competing for the title. The opening match will see defending champions Lumbini Lions take on last season’s runners-up, Sudurpaschim Royals. This season marks a major milestone, with International Cricket Council recognition and the introduction of the Decision Review System, allowing teams to challenge certain umpiring decisions. The tournament will feature international stars, including former Australian captain David Warner, West Indies all-rounder Andre Russell, South African batter David Miller and Bangladesh all-rounder Shakib Al Hasan.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired the 54th meeting of PRAGATI, the ICT-enabled, multi-modal platform aimed at fostering Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation, at Seva Teerth in New Delhi yesterday.During the meeting, the  Prime Minister reviewed infrastructure projects across the Railways, Ekta Malls and Drug Parks worth over 16 thousand crore rupees covering 31 States and Union Territories. Pivotal to economic growth and public welfare, these projects, were reviewed with a focus on timeliness, inter-agency coordination, and timely issue resolution.Prime Minister asked the concerned Ministries and State Governments to resolve bottlenecks in mission mode, strengthen Centre-State and inter-agency coordination, and ensure close monitoring at the senior-most level. Calling for a proactive work culture with greater ownership at every level, he stressed the need to anticipate implementation challenges, take timely decisions and fix clear accountability for completing projects on schedule.Prime Minister Modi also asked Chief Secretaries to review schemes with District Magistrates every month to address implementation gaps and ensure that benefits reach eligible beneficiaries on time. He emphasised that governance must focus on outcomes over outlays, ensuring that public expenditure translates into tangible improvements in people’s lives.Prime Minister Modi stressed that PM Ekta Malls should provide markets for local products, strengthen the livelihoods of artisans and help them expand their enterprises. He emphasised the need for regular review of progress by Chief Secretaries and to ensure timely completion of the malls.Reviewing Bulk Drug Parks in Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and Himachal Pradesh, Mr Modi stressed the need to prioritise domestic production of active pharmaceutical ingredients and essential inputs to strengthen self-reliance.Referring to the Aspirational Districts and Aspirational Blocks Programmes, Mr Modi highlighted the role of convergence, regular monitoring and local accountability in accelerating development in underserved areas. He noted that sustained efforts to strengthen governance and improve the delivery of welfare schemes had helped nearly 25 crore people move out of multidimensional poverty.During the review of the redevelopment of Ahmedabad railway station, Mr Modi called for expediting the redevelopment of major railway stations across the country to improve passenger convenience and ease of travel. He emphasised that redeveloped stations should serve as multimodal transport hubs, with seamless connectivity to metro and other transport networks.

. Indian opener Abhishek Sharma has dethroned compatriot Ishan Kishan to claim the top spot in the latest ICC Men’s T20I batting rankings. Kishan has slipped to third place, while Pakistan’s Sahibzada Farhan has climbed to the second position. Abhishek’s rise to the top came a day after he smashed his fourth T20I century, scoring 113 off just 38 balls against New Zealand in the third T20 International to power India to a six-wicket win. Meanwhile, South Africa’s Marco Jansen has replaced India’s Ravindra Jadeja as the No. 1-ranked Test all-rounder following his impressive all-round performances against Australia in the ongoing Test series.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like GST Council.Introduced on 1STJuly, 2017, the Goods and Services Tax (GST) marked a significant milestone in India’s tax reform journey. By bringing multiple Central and State taxes under a unified framework, GST gave effect to the principle of One Nation, One Tax and paved the way for a more integrated and streamlined taxation system across the country. The proposals of the GST Council seek to create a more predictable and taxpayer-friendly GST registration framework. Under the next-generation GST reforms last year, the GST council had simplified the earlier four-tier structure of 5 per cent, 12 percent, 18 percent, 28 percent into a two tier structure of 5 percent and 18 percent. Addressing the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi today, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that through GST, the government has transformed a complex web of taxes into a national market.Addressing media after the 58thGST Council meeting in New Delhi, Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said that the Council   recommended removing arrest powers under GST, raising the prosecution threshold from one crore to five crore rupees.Over the past nine years, standardised procedures and rationalised rates have supported greater transparency, accountability and economic growth and strengthened the vision of ‘Ek Bharat – Shreshtha Bharat’.

. Indian developers have secured 23 major contracts, accumulating over 5.5 Lakh Million Tonnes Per Annum in supply commitments under the National Green Hydrogen Mission. This information was shared by Minister for New and Renewable EnergyPralhad Joshi in a social media post. Mr Joshi said that over 70% dedicated to global exports, this milestone is driving 90 thousand crore rupees in clean energy investments. He noted that this milestone will accelerate India’s journey toward global net-zero leadership and green job creation.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that the deep depression over East central and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal has moved southeastwards and intensified into a Deep Depression today. IMD added that the deep depression is very likely to move nearly southwestwards, and intensify further into a cyclonic storm over east central adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal by early morning tomorrow. It has advised fishermen not to venture into West Central and adjoining Northwest and Southwest Bay of Bengal during the next two days.The Weather Agency has issued an orange colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall over Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal tomorrow. Heavy Rainfall is also expected over Coastal Andhra Pradesh during the next two days.The Met Department has predictedthunderstormsaccompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Gangetic West Bengal, Kerala, Mahe, Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar Islands during the next two to three days.For Delhi, the IMD has forecast a clear sky tomorrow. The maximum temperature in the National Capital will be around 31 to 33 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature will hover around 15 to 17 degrees Celsius tomorrow.

. India has called for greater representation of women in the armed forces, stating that their participation can strengthen the protection of women and girls affected by conflicts and advance the United Nations’ Women, Peace and Security (WPS) agenda.Speaking at the UN Security Council’s open debate on WPS yesterday, India’s Permanent Representative, P. Harish, cited a UN report stating that 750 million women and girls live within 50 kilometres of conflict zones. He also highlighted that verified cases of conflict-related sexual violence had more than doubled in a year.Harish highlighted the contributions of Indian Army Majors Mouiz Yaseen and Sonia Devendra Nevaskar, who served with the UN Mission in South Sudan and developed initiatives to improve the safety, welfare and participation of women peacekeepers and civilians.He said India had expanded opportunities for women in the armed forces, including permanent commissions and induction into all combat streams. He added that women’s participation in peacekeeping and decision-making was essential to building sustainable peace.Harish also cited the Women’s Reservation Act, 2023, which provides for one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies, as an important step towards greater gender representation in political leadership.

. The Trump administration has said, it is blocking imports from three Chinese biotechnology firms alleging their links to forced labour in China’s Xinjiang region. The Department of Homeland Security today said, the companies sourced materials from Xinjiang or worked with regional authorities to recruit and transfer forced labor involving persecuted ethnic minorities, including Uyghurs. The move comes amid growing US-China competition in biotechnology and follows proposed US restrictions on investments in Chinese biotechnology, artificial intelligence and supercomputing.

. In squash, India’s Anahat Singh has advanced to the quarterfinals of the Canadian Women’s Open squash tournament following a four-game victory over England’s Saran Nghiem.Currently ranked 15th in the world, Anahat defeated 52nd-ranked Saran 11-6, 4-11, 11-5, 11-7 in the second round. Anahat had received a bye in the first round. Anahat will now take on Egypt’s world No. 7 and top seed Fayrouz Aboelkheir in her next match.

. The 9th Hero Hockey Men’s Asian Champions Trophy 2026 has begun at Jalandhar’s Olympian Surjit Hockey Stadium, today, with India routing Bangladesh by 13-0 .Akashvani’s Jalandhar Correspondent reports that earlier, in the first two matches played during day, Malaysia beat China by 5-4, whereas Japan defeated Korea by 3-2.Tomorrow is a rest day. On Thursday, November 29th, India will take on China, Malaysia will play with South Korea whereas Bangladesh will face Japan.Akashvani’s all FM Rainbow Channels along with Jalandhar’s Primary Channel are broadcasting live commentary of matches played between Indian and other teams. The commentary of semi-finals and final will also be available on these channels as well.

. The Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) has extended the New Amnesty Scheme, 2025 till 31st December this year. The scheme which was in effect from 1st October 2025 to 30th September 2026 has been extended for three months on existing terms and conditions. Ministry of Labour and Employment said that with the extension of this Scheme, eligible employers and Insured Persons will have additional time to avail themselves of the benefits of the Scheme.The New Amnesty Scheme 2025 is a one-time dispute resolution initiative aimed at reducing the backlog of court cases and promoting compliance under the erstwhile Employees’ State Insurance Act, 1948 Act. The scheme provides a structured mechanism for employers to resolve legal disputes with ESIC for an out-of-court settlement.

. Global crude oil prices rose ‌over one per cent today amid supply risks after Saudi Arabia’s largest oil refinery was reportedly hit with a missile by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis. Brent crude was trading 1.1 per cent up at 115 US dollars and 16 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading over 1.8 per cent higher at 101 US dollars and 75 cents per barrel.

. Indian wrestlers Neelam Sirohi and Kajal Dhochak clinched silver medals in their respective categories at the World Wrestling Championships in Astana, Kazakhstan, today. The 26-year-old Neelam lost 5-nil to Japanese wrestling legend Yui Susaki in the women’s 50kg final to secure the silver medal. Meanwhile, Kajal also settled for silver after suffering a narrow 8-6 defeat to Ukraine’s Anastasiya Alpyeyeva in the 76kg final. With this achievement, Neelam and Kajal join Anshu Malik as the only Indian women wrestlers to have won silver medals at the global showpiece.

. The Union Cabinet has approved the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme to promote domestic manufacturing.The total outlay for the scheme is ten thousand crore rupees for 13 years upto Financial Year 2039-40. The scheme aims to establish a globally competitive container manufacturing ecosystem in India, reduce import dependence and strengthen supply chain resilience.Briefing media after the Union Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the scheme is intended to support new manufacturing facilities as well as expansion of existing container manufacturing units.He said, it has four components including Interest Subvention Assistance, Testing and Certification assistance, Land Leasing support and Operational Expenditure Assistance. Mr Vaishnaw added that the scheme will create an internationally competitive manufacturing base, with potential to position India as a global export hub for quality shipping containers.The  Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme will strengthen resilience of India’s maritime and logistics supply chains. It will generate an estimated 3,000 direct jobs and over 50,000 indirect jobs, while supporting ancillary industries such as corner castings, specialised steel, wooden frames and paints.Mr Vaishnaw informed that Union Cabinet also approved  three percent  increase in Dearness Allowance to Central Government employees and Dearness Relief to Pensioners with effect from 1st of July,2026. Mr Vaishnaw added that this will benefit over  48 lakh Central Government employees and 68 lakh pensioners.The Union Cabinet has also approved the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme to position India as a global hub for high-quality sports goods. Giving details about the scheme ,   Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that  that the scheme has an approved outlay of over  one thousand 856 crore rupees over eight years period  from 2026-27 to 2033-34. He said, the scheme will support the development of a globally competitive sports goods industry and strengthen India’s position in global supply chains.Mr Vaishnaw said that the  Scheme envisages the development of dedicated Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones (SGMZs) to promote cluster-based manufacturing and create integrated industrial ecosystems. Mr Vaishnaw added that  incentives and interventions are the two parts of the scheme where incentive supports manufacturing while intervetion builds the wider ecosystem.The Union Minister also said that a key focus of the Scheme is to attract new investments and strengthen domestic manufacturing capacity in the sports goods sector. The Anchor Investment Support component will encourage leading domestic and global manufacturers, brands and retail chains to establish manufacturing facilities within designated Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones and foster the development of robust supplier and ancillary ecosystems. Complementing this, the Turnover Linked Support component will incentivise higher production, capacity expansion and sustained manufacturing growth.Mr Vaishnaw also informed that the Union Cabinet has approved the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana (PMVGSY) scheme as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme. It aims to transform Panchayats into empowered, self-reliant, accountable and high-performing institutions of local self-government, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat.Mr Vaishnaw said that the scheme has a total financial outlay of 7,395 crore rupees and the duration of the scheme  is for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31. He said, the scheme applies to all States and Union Territories, including rural local governance institutions in non-Part IX areas where Panchayats do not exist. It will cover more than 2.78 lakh Rural Local Bodies and Traditional Bodies across the country. Mr Vaishnaw said, around 32 lakh elected representatives, along with Panchayat functionaries and other stakeholders, across over 2.55 lakh Panchayats and Traditional Local Bodies will be direct beneficiaries of the scheme.The combined impact on the exchequer on account of increase in both Dearness Allowance and Dearness Relief would be over 10,000 crore rupees  per annum.

. The United States and Japan have agreed to jointly produce advanced medium-range air-to-air missiles at a facility in Japan. Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said the project, dubbed Operation Supercharge will produce missiles essential for F-35 fighter jets.Mr. Koizumi said this after meeting US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth in Cebu, Philippines, on the sidelines of a regional defence meeting. The two officials agreed to strengthen their alliance’s deterrence and response capabilities amid growing regional security concerns, Koizumi said, without naming any specific country. Hegseth separately reaffirmed Washington’s commitment to defending its allies and deterring aggression in the Indo-Pacific. He also assured Philippine officials of US support amid tensions with China in the disputed South China Sea.

. Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said India plans to increase its port capacity fourfold by 2047 to support economic growth andexpandinginternational trade. Speaking in Rotterdam during his visit to the Netherlands, Mr Goyal said, India had doubled its port capacity over the past decade and aims to quadruple it over the next two decades. He highlighted opportunities for cooperation with the Port of Rotterdam in the Netherlands in maritime infrastructure, green energy, carbon capture and sustainable trade.The Minister emphasised the importance of cooperation with the Port of Rotterdam in modernising existing ports, developing world-class infrastructure and improving operational efficiency. Highlighting the government’s Sagarmala initiative, the Minister said efforts were underway to expand port infrastructure and improve maritime connectivity.The Minister expressed confidence that stronger cooperation with major international maritime hubs such as Rotterdam would help India expand its maritime capabilities and strengthen its role in global trade.Describing India as the world’s fastest-growing major economy, Mr Goyal said the country had made significant progress in quality, efficiency and productivity, strengthening its position in global trade and logistics.
